## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
#EXPLORING THE DATASET
library(tidyverse)

netflix <- read.csv("netflix_customer_churn.csv")

View(netflix)

head(netflix)

glimpse(netflix)

summary(netflix)
```

```{r}
#Descriptive statistics
descriptive_stats <- netflix %>%
  mutate(
    churn_status = if_else(churned == 1, "Churned", "Stayed")
  ) %>%
  group_by(churn_status) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    
    mean_watch_hours = mean(watch_hours, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_watch_hours = median(watch_hours, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_watch_hours = sd(watch_hours, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    mean_last_login = mean(last_login_days, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_last_login = median(last_login_days, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_last_login = sd(last_login_days, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    mean_profiles = mean(number_of_profiles, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_profiles = median(number_of_profiles, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_profiles = sd(number_of_profiles, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    mean_daily_watch = mean(avg_watch_time_per_day, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_daily_watch = median(avg_watch_time_per_day, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_daily_watch = sd(avg_watch_time_per_day, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2)
  ) %>%
  relocate(percentage, .after = n)

descriptive_stats
```

```{r}
# Proportion for the categorical variable subscription_type
churn_subscription <- netflix %>%
  group_by(subscription_type) %>%
  summarise(
    churn_rate = mean(churned) * 100
  )

churn_subscription
```

```{r}
#VISUALIZATION 1: probability of churn by watch hours
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(netflix, aes(x = watch_hours, y = churned)) +
  geom_jitter(color = "grey60",
              alpha = 0.3,
              width = 0,
              height = 0.05,
              size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "glm",
              method.args = list(family = binomial),
              se = FALSE,
              color = "blue",
              linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Watch Hours vs Customer Churn",
       x = "Watch Hours",
       y = "Probability of Churn") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#VISUALIZATION 2: watch hours by churn
netflix %>%
  mutate(
    churn_status = if_else(
      churned == 1,
      "Churned",
      "Stayed"
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = churn_status,
      y = watch_hours
    )
  ) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Watch Hours by Customer Churn",
    x = "Customer Status",
    y = "Watch Hours"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#VISUALIZATION 3: days since last login

netflix %>%

```

```{r}
#VISUALIZATION 4: customer churn by subscription type
netflix <- netflix %>%
  mutate(
    churn_status = if_else(
      churned == 1,
      "Churned",
      "Not Churned"
    )
  )

ggplot(
  netflix,
  aes(
    x = subscription_type,
    fill = churn_status
  )
) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Churned" = "tomato",
      "Not Churned" = "steelblue"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Customer Churn by Subscription Type",
    x = "Subscription Type",
    y = "Percentage of Customers",
    fill = "Customer Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Singularity involving monthly_fee and subscription_type
FeeModel <- lm(
  monthly_fee ~ subscription_type,
  data = netflix
)

summary(FeeModel)
```

```{r}
# Multicollinearity check for watch_hours and avg_watch_time_per_day
cor(
  netflix$watch_hours,
  netflix$avg_watch_time_per_day
)
```

```{r}
#FULL MODEL
FullModel <- glm(
  churned ~ age +
    gender +
    subscription_type +
    watch_hours +
    last_login_days +
    region +
    device +
    monthly_fee +
    payment_method +
    number_of_profiles +
    avg_watch_time_per_day +
    favorite_genre,
  data = netflix,
  family = binomial
)

summary(FullModel)
```

```{r}
# MODEL A
ModelA <- glm(
  churned ~ subscription_type +
    watch_hours +
    last_login_days +
    payment_method +
    number_of_profiles +
    avg_watch_time_per_day,
  data = netflix,
  family = binomial
)

summary(ModelA)
```

```{r}
# MODEL B
ModelB <- glm(
  churned ~ subscription_type +
    watch_hours +
    last_login_days +
    payment_method +
    number_of_profiles +
    avg_watch_time_per_day +
    gender,
  data = netflix,
  family = binomial
)

summary(ModelB)
```

```{r}
# MODEL C
ModelC <- glm(
  churned ~ subscription_type +
    watch_hours +
    last_login_days +
    number_of_profiles +
    avg_watch_time_per_day,
  data = netflix,
  family = binomial
)

summary(ModelC)
```

```{r}
# MODEL COMPARISON: AIC AND BIC

model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Full Model", "Model A", "Model B", "Model C"),
  
  AIC = c(
    AIC(FullModel),
    AIC(ModelA),
    AIC(ModelB),
    AIC(ModelC)
  ),
  
  BIC = c(
    BIC(FullModel),
    BIC(ModelA),
    BIC(ModelB),
    BIC(ModelC)
  )
)

model_comparison$AIC <- round(model_comparison$AIC, 2)
model_comparison$BIC <- round(model_comparison$BIC, 2)

model_comparison
```

```{r}
# COEFFICIENTS AND ODDS RATIO (MODEL B)
ModelB <- glm(
  churned ~ subscription_type +
    watch_hours +
    last_login_days +
    payment_method +
    number_of_profiles +
    avg_watch_time_per_day +
    gender,
  data = netflix,
  family = binomial
)

summary(ModelB)

# Calculate Odds Ratios
exp(coef(ModelB))

OR_table <- data.frame(
  Predictor = names(coef(ModelB)),
  Coefficient = round(coef(ModelB), 3),
  Odds_Ratio = round(exp(coef(ModelB)), 3),
  P_value = signif(summary(ModelB)$coefficients[, 4], 3)
)

OR_table

```
